I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the data layout.

Output was truncated in the middle; reading the omitted parts.

My last call was malformed. I'll look at the rest of the codebook.

Now I have the rules. Writing the script.

That call was malformed again, so I'll write the file with `write_file`.

`/app/bin/crosstabs.py` is written, and I ran it on `/app/data` to produce `/app/out/tables.json`.

- **Checks:** `python tools/check_tables.py` reports that every figure matches the approved tables. The summary and all six tables match. `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` ran 4 tests, all passing.
- **How it works:** the script follows the rules in `/app/docs` rather than anything specific to the current files. It uses only the standard library and doesn't touch `/app/data`, `/app/docs`, `/app/tests` or `/app/tools`.
- **Unspecified edge cases:**
  - A partial row with no `last_page` value counts as page 0.
  - Two rows of one respondent with the same status and the same instant keep the first one read, with files taken in name order.
  - A raking category whose weights have all gone to zero gets a factor of 1.

  These cases aren't covered by the docs or the tests.

`/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f | grep -v '^./.git/' | head -100; cat docs/overview.md; wc -c docs/*
cd /app/docs; cat exports.md codebook.md cleaning.md weighting.md tables.md output.md changelog.md
cd /app/docs; sed -n '/^## 5. Routing/,$p' codebook.md; cat cleaning.md; cat weighting.md

cd /app; cat data/codebook.json | head -150; cat data/weighting.json data/tables.json data/exports/export_log.txt; head -3 data/exports/*.csv; cat tools/check_tables.py | head -50; sed -n 1,60p tests/test_tables.py

cd /app; python3 - <<'E'
import json
c=json.load(open('data/codebook.json'))
for q in c['questions'][2:]:
    print(json.dumps(q))
E
cd /app; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/crosstabs.py data out/tables.json && python tools/check_tables.py; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -20

cd /app; echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Wrote /app/bin/crosstabs.py implementing the documented reading, cleaning, raking/trimming and crosstab rules, and saved the result to /app/out/tables.json. check_tables.py reports every figure matches and the 4 unit tests pass."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
